independent.summary: Pre-existing: GalleryBlock is the one block type with no inline editor at all — it declares `canEdit` but never renders a pencil and emits no `save`, so BlockList's `@save="data => saveBlock(block, data)"` on it is dead wiring (and now lands as a stray `onSave` DOM-event listener on its root). Since EntityEditor only opens for new entities (WikiLayout.vue:1550 `mode: 'editor'` is reached only via openEditor/openNewEntity), a gallery block added to an existing entity through "+ Add block" can never be given images from the UI; it renders "No images yet." permanently and can only be deleted. This change converted the four editable block types to the `onSave` function-prop convention and left gallery as the odd one out, which also makes the item's cited refusal scenario ("a 400 from blockDataError on a gallery URL" raised by a block editor) unreachable from a block editor.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication or authorization logic changes — `canWrite`/`canEdit`/`blockEditable` gating and the server-side role check are untouched; only the client's UI reaction to an already-refused write changed.
No credentials, tokens or env handling; the only new logging (`inlineEdit.js` verbose tier) emits user-typed block/header content and is gated off below verbose.
Nothing billing-, pricing- or quota-related appears in the diff.
The change removes a data-loss path rather than adding one; the `deleteBlock` edit in EntityDetail.vue is a pure emit→function-prop invocation refactor with identical delete semantics.
No new or altered outbound calls — the only request involved is the app's own `PUT /entities/:id` via the existing `editEntity`, whose call site is unchanged.
No version bumps, build/deploy config, migrations or dependency changes; the only non-code edit is a Decision Log paragraph in kol_emet_spec.md.

summary: The local review found nothing, and there is genuinely almost nothing to find — the function-prop conversion is complete and consistent, the chain returns `true` only after `editEntity` resolves, and all 52+123 affected client tests pass — so its clean pass and correct triage are defensible, though it missed the one real (pre-existing) gap that GalleryBlock has no inline editor at all.
